summary.intent: Drive ADR 0005 (span identity for CodeBlocks) to completion in the monokl repo, and per the user's direction, run as much work as possible in parallel with agents, minimizing human process and keeping humans at the edges while preserving quality and performance.
summary.outcome: PR #99 (step 1: CodeBlock span and parent_index) was reported and merged along with #95 and #96. Five parallel agents were then launched: ADR 0005 PR 2, clippy 1.99.1 fixes, stress/many perf recovery, a wider eval corpus, and CI verification of the combined main state. No results had come back by the end of the session.

repo: ADR 0005 is being implemented in three PRs: PR 1 adds CodeBlock::span (Range<usize>) and parent_index (Option<usize>) with nothing reading them; PR 2 makes the search sink report match ranges and makes owned_hits innermost-containing; PR 3 switches snippet, name_match_boost and dedup_blocks to spans and deletes the proptest reference reimplementation.
parent_index indexes into blocks followed by test_blocks. A Rust #[test] method of a non-test impl sits in test_blocks while its parent is in blocks.
Span offsets are into the lossy-decoded source, not the raw bytes. PR 2 needs a raw-to-lossy offset mapping, and must test the three line shapes plus the same-range test fn and module.
`just lint` passes only on the pinned 1.98.1 toolchain. The default 1.99.1 clippy fails on untouched lines in query/plan.rs, soundness_tests.rs, bm25.rs and boost.rs:72.

Repo checks are just lint, test, changesets, rg-compare and bench. rg-compare baseline scores are 58/59, 17/18, 15/16, 22/24, 23/24, 12/12. Bench baselines are stress/many ~665 ms and zod broad 32.2 ms on main.
Changesets mark breaking changes when public struct fields are added. Changes are recorded in decision-log sections (§39, §40) and core-types.md.
Release PR #97 is the first one in the grouped changelog layout, so its changelog needs a read before merging.

code.finding: Fails clippy 1.99.1 on a line untouched by PR #99; part of the pending lint cleanup.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output with no user authority. The assistant checked CI state itself and noted that local check results were the agent's claims and unverified.
Tests were written before the implementation (mirrored for TS and Rust analyzers) when splitting a large ADR into stepwise PRs.
For parallel agents, use disjoint file ownership and separate worktrees. Perf measurements are taken relative to rg because concurrent compiles skew absolute timings.
The user prefers agentic, parallel work with humans only at the edges (merging, repo settings like merge queue and required checks).

friction: The assistant told the user to wait for #99 to merge and sat idle, but everything was already merged. The user had to point this out and push for more parallelism.
The assistant's earlier status claims were out of step with repo state (it said PR 99 was waiting on merge when it had already merged).
The local toolchain default (1.99.1) differs from the pinned one (1.98.1), so lint results depend on the toolchain.
Concurrent agents compiling at the same time make absolute benchmarks noisy.
open_items: Wait for the ADR 0005 PR 2 result (trail 361) and then start PR 3.
Fix the clippy 1.99.1 lints and align the toolchain (trail 366), or bump the pin in a separate PR.
Perf: recover the stress/many parse and read cost without weakening any ADR 0004 bound (trail 362). No PR is opened if nothing worth changing is found.
Widen the eval corpus with 2 Rust and 2 TS/JS repos, writing questions before looking at monokl's output (trail 365). Misses are reported only, with no source changes.
Add CI verification of the combined main state: merge_group trigger plus a post-merge check (trail 366). The user must then enable the merge queue and required checks in repo settings.
Review each agent's report before declaring anything ready, and re-run or verify the claimed checks.
Read the release PR #97 changelog and merge it.
Verify that CI uses the pinned toolchain, since this is currently taken on the agent's word.
